public_rationale: He said the demand reflected in supplier guidance like NVIDIA's is "almost-entirely funded by debt." That demand comes largely from big hyperscalers. In Q1 2026, Alphabet's operating cash flow was $45.8B against $35.7B of capex. Meta generated $32.2B of operating cash flow and still had $12.4B of free cash flow after capex. Both paid for their buildouts out of operating cash. Debt did grow: Alphabet issued $31.1B of notes that quarter. But debt was not almost the whole source of funding for these major buyers. On the plain reading, the claim is contradicted. The result depends on reading "that demand" as the broad demand behind supplier guidance. If he meant only third-party data center projects funded by private credit, debt may well dominate there, but I found no aggregate figure for that segment.
limitations: Only two hyperscalers checked, for one quarter. Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, neoclouds and AI labs were not quantified.
Cash is fungible. Some debt raised may indirectly support capex even when operating cash flow exceeds capex.
A narrower reading limited to private-credit data center deals could come out differently.

our_interpretation: "That demand" refers to the AI compute and data center demand shown in supplier guidance such as NVIDIA's. That demand comes mostly from hyperscalers and large AI buyers.
Plain reading: "almost entirely funded by debt" means debt pays for the large majority (roughly 80-90% or more) of spending on AI compute and data centers, not operating cash flow or equity.

He names no period. The claim describes an ongoing state at the post date, so the target period is 1 January 2026 to the post date. That covers the latest quarters reported before the post (calendar Q1 2026, and NVIDIA's quarter ending April 2026).
If the largest buyers paid for most of their capital spending out of operating cash flow in that period, the claim is false on this reading.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that most spending on AI compute and data centers in early 2026, including by the largest hyperscaler buyers, was paid for with borrowed money rather than operating cash flow or equity.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that major buyers behind that demand (for example Alphabet and Meta) paid for their capital spending in early 2026 mainly out of operating cash flow, so debt was not almost the whole source of funding.
